Patch release for the Trigora CLI.

## Fixed

- `trigora start` with no `--input` now passes an empty argument list. `--input '{}'` is still treated as one object argument.
- Rust effect scaffolding no longer treats text inside string and character literals as captured bindings.
- `trigora init --language rust` now prints the correct Cargo package name in the next-step commands.
- Cloud commands now consistently target the project configured in `trigora.toml`, including deploy and remote execution commands.
- `trigora inspect` and execution lists display `programName` when available.

- Require TCC Engine 26.10.3.
- Python support is now CPython 3.10–3.14. New Python projects and the `trigora-cli` wheel declare that range.

## Packages

This release updates:

### Changed
- README: a quarter less prose, every section kept, the jokes too. Visuals first: real-app scenes, looks and creative arrows now come right after the hero, before the use-case list and the reference.
- Skill: 36% fewer tokens (SKILL.md 2,182 to 1,398, counted with Anthropic's token-count API), every rule kept, following the [Agent Skills best practices](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/best-practices): one worked example instead of prose, rarely needed detail (System Settings pane ids, Chrome page coordinates, look and timing flags) moved to `skill/big-arrow/reference.md`, loaded only when needed.

The prebuilt binary is signed ad hoc, not notarized: Gatekeeper blocks it when it is downloaded with a browser (remove the quarantine flag with xattr -d com.apple.quarantine bigarrow). Installing with Homebrew builds from source and avoids this.

### Changed
- README hero: a real desktop again (menu bar, Dock, a normal Chrome window with tabs and address bar) with nine arrows on the 2014-06-10 Hacker News front page, every one a different colour, shape or style, from every side, no headline covered. `scripts/hn-scene.sh` records it on the main display, no virtual display.
- README "Real apps, real use cases": every scene shows other looks (rings, boxes, zigzags, sharp corners, close button, white-black border, hex colours), most with a second or third arrow, and the menu bar is in every shot. `scripts/real-scenes.sh` crops to the main display's size, hides other Finder windows and reads the two version-dependent labels from `SETTINGS_ADD` and `FINDER_ICONS`.

The prebuilt binary is signed ad hoc, not notarized: Gatekeeper blocks it when it is downloaded with a browser (remove the quarantine flag with xattr -d com.apple.quarantine bigarrow). Installing with Homebrew builds from source and avoids this.

After the [Hacker News thread](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50018817); triage in `docs/feedback/2026-10-09-hacker-news.md`.

### Fixed
- The box or ring around the target no longer drifts while it pulses: its layer scaled around the display's centre, so a box near a corner swam up to 55 pt off its target and back. Found by @jarombouts in #37 (#38).
- `--window` on a window left half off every display (after unplugging one) points at its visible part instead of failing with "outside every display".

### Changed
- Skill: when a click approves, grants, pays, signs, sends or deletes something, the sign says what happens (#42).
- Skill: open the exact System Settings pane or page first, then point; deep links verified on macOS 27 (#43, research in `docs/research/2026-10-09-system-settings-deep-links.md`).
- Permission errors name the pane macOS shows: on macOS 27 the Accessibility list is titled "Device Control and Data Access".
- README: plain-language tagline and permissions FAQ, new FAQ entries on focus, trust and token cost, use cases that lead with guiding and helping (#39, #44).
- New guide, `docs/guides/allow-screen-recording/`: how to allow screen recording on a Mac, six steps along Apple's own path, every screenshot a real arrow drawn by an agent on macOS 27, including the real password sheet.
- GitHub's language stats ignore `scripts/`; the binary is Swift only (#45).
- README: "Real apps, real use cases" with five real-app scenes recorded on macOS 27 by `scripts/real-scenes.sh` (System Settings, Keynote, TextEdit, Chrome, Finder) (#40); the hero is re-staged on a 2014 front page with short arrows that cross no headline (#41); the staged dialogs moved further down into "Creative arrows", one image per row.

The prebuilt binary is signed ad hoc, not notarized: Gatekeeper blocks it when it is downloaded with a browser (remove the quarantine flag with xattr -d com.apple.quarantine bigarrow). Installing with Homebrew builds from source and avoids this.

## [6.3.0](https://github.com/morluto/rea/compare/rea-agents-6.2.0...rea-agents-6.3.0) (2026-10-09)


### ⚠ BREAKING CHANGES

* **captures:** Historical captures without current producer accounting or transaction identity, and web diffs missing accessibility or storage dimensions, are rejected. Preserve original captures and recapture with the current producer; update comparison consumers to include every dimension rather than synthesizing missing observations. See the [process capture guide](docs/process-capture.md) and [browser scenario contract](docs/browser-scenario-contract.md). ([3283a45](https://github.com/morluto/rea/commit/3283a45d09457c79e3adadb50a48620926d4bc5b))

* **contracts:** Provider analysis outputs must explicitly supply metadata previously repaired with defaults; unsupported nullable facets must be reported as null.
* **javascript:** Semantic graph facts now store evidence context IDs and locations. Graph and semantic trace results require an inline evidence_contexts table.

## What's new in 1.6.4 "Hex, patch 4"

- On a night when the Moon stays below the horizon, the popover's Moon tile reads "Down" with "tonight" under it, where "Down tonight" on one line was broken in the middle of the word

## Install

Download `Nightwatch-1.6.4.dmg` below, open it and drag Nightwatch to Applications. It is signed with a Developer ID and notarised by Apple. The first time you open it, macOS asks whether to open an app downloaded from the internet: choose Open. Its SHA-256 checksum is in `Nightwatch-1.6.4.dmg.sha256`.

If the desktop widget shows only grey bars after you replace an older copy, macOS is still holding the old version on record: the [Desktop widget section of the README](https://github.com/rsutcliffe/nightwatch#desktop-widget-optional) has the two Terminal commands that clear it.

From 0.6.7 on, Nightwatch checks once a day for a newer version and says so in its popover. Questions and ideas: [Discussions](https://github.com/rsutcliffe/nightwatch/discussions). Problems: [Issues](https://github.com/rsutcliffe/nightwatch/issues).

- Once Apple Weather has answered on this Mac, a forecast that had to come from Open-Meteo is replaced after five minutes, where it used to stay for thirty, so the Apple Weather forecast is back soon after Apple answers again
- The privacy policy link is in the welcome and at the foot of Settings, and no longer a second time in About, which opens from the foot of Settings

Engine: file-name segments and bracket notation address whole map entries

A state path segment that names a file or URL (starts with / or ~/, or
contains ://) absorbs the segments after it, so world.files./app/report.txt
is the entry /app/report.txt rather than a nested txt key: existing keys are
matched longest-first, an object value writes the whole entry, a scalar
value names the last segment as an attribute. Bracket notation
(world.files["/app/report.txt"]) is normalized to the dotted form when a
mutation is built and when a path is resolved.

Before this, a model's `delete world.files./app/report.txt` after a
`merge` that created the proper key was a silent no-op (the file survived
`mv`), and bracket paths were rejected as undeclared, dropping the effects.
Regression test added; the reproduction guide notes that the reported runs
predate the fix and how much of the tracker's mutations it affected.

﻿Security fixes, a leaner MCP server, and any currency you like.

**Upgrade recommended.** v1.1.0 fixes a stored XSS on the dashboard and a login open redirect.

## Security
- **Dashboard XSS fixed.** Goal titles, categories, metrics and finance category names are now escaped before rendering. These values can be written through the API, so this was the most important fix. (#20)
- **Login open redirect fixed.** After sign-in, `redirect` must be a same-origin path. (#20)
- **Habittify CSRF.** Habittify write requests now need the session's CSRF token, like every other write endpoint. (#21)
- **Sign-in rate limit.** After 5 failed attempts from one client in 15 minutes, sign-in returns `429` with `Retry-After`. (#21)
- **Security headers.** `Content-Security-Policy`, `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN`, `Referrer-Policy` and `X-Content-Type-Options` are now sent on every response. (#21)
- **HTTPS behind a reverse proxy.** The new `LIFEOS_TRUST_PROXY` setting marks the session cookie `Secure` from `X-Forwarded-Proto` and rate-limits per real client IP. (#21)

Thanks to everyone who reviewed the code after the launch. The findings are tracked in #19.

## MCP server
- **One `lifeos_query` tool for all reads.** The 12 read-only tools are now a single tool with a `type` (`dashboard`, `goals`, `tasks`, `habits`, `finance_summary`, `notes` and so on). Fewer tools means less context used in every conversation. (#17)

## New
- **Display currency.** Choose your currency in Settings: Toman, Rial, USD, EUR, GBP, AED, TRY, CAD, AUD, CHF, JPY, CNY or INR. Amounts are labels only and are never converted. (#22)
- **Landing page** at https://edrisranjbar.github.io/lifeos/ (#18)

## Fixes and polish
- Goals: a goal without a checklist no longer blanks the page.
- Kanban: Escape or an empty title discards a new card.
- Simpler Growth page and Goals cards, and a clearer menu order. (#7)
- README demo GIF, website link and badges. (#23)
- Light-theme screenshots in the README. (#15, thanks @ChirayuPoddar)

## For self-hosters
- **Docker health check.** `docker compose ps` now reports healthy/unhealthy once the app is actually serving. (#16, thanks @aryann2611)
- **CI** runs the PHP and Node test suites on every pull request. (#14, thanks @Mathi23ok)
- Contributing guide, issue templates and PR template. (#8)

## Upgrading
1. Pull or download the new release and restart. The new `login_throttle` table is created automatically; no manual migration is needed.
2. **Behind a TLS reverse proxy** (Caddy, Traefik, nginx): set `LIFEOS_TRUST_PROXY=true` in `.env`, or `'trust_proxy' => true` in `config.php`. Leave it `false` if the app is reachable directly.
3. **MCP clients:** update `mcp/` and restart your client. Prompts that named an old read tool (for example `lifeos_list_goals`) now go through `lifeos_query`.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/edrisranjbar/lifeos/compare/v1.0.0...v1.1.0

## What's Changed
* Add LifeOS API and MCP integration by @edrisranjbar in https://github.com/edrisranjbar/lifeos/pull/1
* LifeOS API, MCP server, Growth workspace and README overhaul by @edrisranjbar in https://github.com/edrisranjbar/lifeos/pull/2
* One-command install (Docker, release zip) and shareable review image by @edrisranjbar in https://github.com/edrisranjbar/lifeos/pull/3
* Separate debts and credits in Finance, one-time or recurring by @edrisranjbar in https://github.com/edrisranjbar/lifeos/pull/4
* Add MIT license by @edrisranjbar in https://github.com/edrisranjbar/lifeos/pull/5

## New Contributors
